text_fidelity_a: Pussan Toys for 6+ Year Old Boys Car, Amphibious Remote Control Car, 2.4 GHz RC Stunt Car Toys 4WD Off-Road Trucks, Birthday Gift for 6-12 Kids Boys Girls, Beach and Water Toys for Children This is a fun 4wd car to drive.  It runs pretty fast on the 6 volt NiCd battery.  It is nearly impossible to roll it over and get it stuck as it just flips over and keeps on going.  Battery life is good (20 to 30 mins).  Controller is a bit small for adult hands but fits my 12 year old granddaughter hands very well.  The car is not DIgitally controlled (its all on or all off- no proportional steering or throttle), but it is able to spin around while staying in place (think tank or dozer like and you get the idea).  Have not had a chance to run it in the water yet as it has been real dry here the last couple weeks.  I tested it on a mowed lawn and gravel driveway and it will handle these surfaces ok.  The plastic tires are getting a little chewed up from the gravel so do be aware that a constant gravel use will probably wear out the tires.  Also tried it on wood and carpet and it runs great on those surfaces.  It comes with a handy phillips screwdriver to take out the 4 (YES 4!) battery cover screws.  I'm guessing so many screws to help keep the battery dry when running in water.  Didn't try out the charging cord as the USB cords are nothing more than a trickle charger and take too long.  I used my B6 V2 chargerer and the battery comes out a little under spec (typical).  Remote takes 2 AA batteries.  Car is fun but there is no suspension and hard plastic tires make for a very stiff drive.  I normally run off road rock crawlers in a dry creek bed so this car really isn't designed for that type of use, but for smooth surface running this is a good fun choice.
text_fidelity_b: Pussan Toys for 6+ Year Old Boys Car, Amphibious Remote Control Car, 2.4 GHz RC Stunt Car Toys 4WD Off-Road Trucks, Birthday Gift for 6-12 Kids Boys Girls, Beach and Water Toys for Children

Battat - Deluxe Wooden Train – Classic Toy Train Set with Magnetic Trains, Tracks, Vehicles, Buildings & Accessories for Kids Aged 3 & Up (102Pc), Fits Thomas, Brio, Chuggington Trains are a classic toy. Most of them are electronic, high- tech in nature, and can be made to look and sound like an authentic train, in small scale of course. But there is also something to be said for a train that isn’t electronic and requires imagination more than anything. This is what you get with the Battat Deluxe Wooden Train.

This train set comes with track, train, and a large number of accessories. It’s easy to assemble the track because it interlocks with almost no effort. Setting up the accessories takes time, but this is perfect for the more imaginative child and parents will enjoy just sitting back and letting their youngster take over.

The quality level of this set is good and the pieces are made from wood. Once assembled, it covers about four feet by three feet of space, so it will fit on most tables. If you don’t have available table space to spare, just set it up on the floor instead. A smooth surface is best, of course, but a flat carpet may work, too.

With the train cars, they are held together by magnets and this is good enough for this type of train. One issue some people may have is with the track. The interlocking isn’t very secure and that means the track is easy to bump out of place. Metal tracks hold together better, but this isn’t a huge issue, really. Most kids won’t mind this aspect of the set up.

There are some really cool electronic trains on the market, but trains that require manual movements and that lack sound and other automated features can be just as fun. The Battat Deluxe Wooden Train is good for this purpose. It’s made with a good deal of quality in mind and it’s great for stimulating a child’s imagination.
text_fidelity_b: Battat - Deluxe Wooden Train – Classic Toy Train Set with Magnetic Trains, Tracks, Vehicles, Buildings & Accessories for Kids Aged 3 & Up (102Pc), Fits Thomas, Brio, Chuggington

Baby Alive Lulu Achoo Doll, 12-Inch Interactive Doctor Play Toy with Lights, Sounds, Movements and Tools, Kids 3 and Up, Brown Hair This baby alive doll was an excellent find. From the moment I pulled her out of the Amazon box, she has been my youngest new favorite thing. It's been a couple of weeks now and my daughter still carries her around the house all day long. I was worried some of the features would get "old" and then soon we just have another doll to add to the toy pile. Lucky, that hasn't happened the thrill hasn't worn off. This achoo doll is very captivating.
This doll's features are just to cute too. When her cute little button nose turns pink, even I can barely stand it... my instincts tell me to go fix it, lol. Needless to say, my daughter absolutely loves taking care of her sick baby. It's the diagnosing and healing her baby's ailments with medicine that is very rewarding. Plus, all the accessories that come with a doll are cute too.
But what I like the best about the doll is she is inspiring additional pretend play. My daughter has pulled out her doctor kit far more often and is inventing other problems to fix, lol. Over all it's a really cute doll and my daughter is getting her money's worth. I probably wouldn't recommend this for a very young toddler or as a child's first baby doll. The achoo version is little big and clunky in comparison, and doesn't feel like a traditional newborn baby doll. That's not to say that I don't recommend this one because I certainly do. It just feels like a step up from the first round of baby doll to me. But even then, I bet kids who aren't into swaddling and carrying around newborn baby dolls, would still love this because of the interactive features. And even cut my older preteen boys playing with it, so kids of any age do enjoy it!
Hope this review is helpful.

text_fidelity_a: Chompin' Charlie Game - Feed The Squirrel Acorns And Race To Collect Them When They Scatter - Includes 24-Piece Puzzle by Goliath This is a perfect addition to the Fall basket. There are always lots of books about squirrels and acorns to add to the fall line-up and this game goes with them well. It's a great companion to those books and we've all had fun with it. There's also a little puzzle to go with the game, which adds more fun to the squirrel/acorn focus. To play the game, the players take turns rolling a die. The color/number that is rolled is what color and how many(up to 2) acorns you put into Charlie's mouth. Once he gets full, the acorns roll out the holes that are in the tree trunk that Charlie stands on. Using only one hand, the players race to collect the acorns. The first player to fill up their acorn stash card wins. The rules say that if a player rolls a certain color and it's not in the main stash of acorns, that player has to take one of their collected acorns or take one from another player. Taking from another player won't be for all families, but it can be adapted, if desired. Also, with the acorns rolling everywhere, it's tricky finding the best place to play. The acorns will roll off the table, but if on the floor, they could roll under things, like couches, if it's a smaller space. Our home is small, so we try to put up little "walls" to make sure the acorns don't roll under things. Overall, it's a fun game and the quality of it is nice, too. It's a simple game that's a great way to add a bit of joy to a day.
text_fidelity_b: Chompin' Charlie Game - Feed The Squirrel Acorns And Race To Collect Them When They Scatter - Includes 24-Piece Puzzle by Goliath

text_fidelity_a: WEQIN Water Guns for Kids Adults 1200CC Squirt Guns High 3 Nozzles Capacity Water Blaster Water Toys Summer Gun Toys Water Shooter Fighting Games Play Toys… This is a great way to cool off in the heat with the kids! My little ones loved how easy it was to replenish after using up the tank (the entire back opens up so it fills much faster), and the triple-nozzle front was a blast (literally! ha). One thing I didn't realize beforehand, however, is that it works entirely by pump action. That is, unlike a super soaker or other water pistol that builds pressure with the pump and then releases with a trigger, the pump is the entire firing mechanism, and the "trigger" is just for show (doesn't do anything). Pulling back on the pump fires the water, and the strength is adjusted  by how hard/fast you pull back. My older kids were able to figure that out, but my youngest (3 years old) found it disappointing. He likes the trigger kind because it is easy for him to fire, and with this he wasn't able to figure out the dexterity to make it shoot very far. For what it is, it works and is fun, but I do sort of wish it had a trigger that wasn't just there for looks.
text_fidelity_b: WEQIN Water Guns for Kids Adults 1200CC Squirt Guns High 3 Nozzles Capacity Water Blaster Water Toys Summer Gun Toys Water Shooter Fighting Games Play Toys…

text_fidelity_a:
Syma 3 Channel S107 Mini Indoor Co-Axial Metal Body Frame & Built-in Gyroscope Helicopter (Color May Vary) I see I'm not the only buyer whose S107 copter arrived DOA. Followed charging instructions to the letter. The copter LEDs lit up when turned on but the remote's LEDs remained lifeless despite tested batteries, double checked for proper placement and connections. Non-functional remote means: copter rotors won't even turn. Never got to see it fly.

The "3 Channel" remote has a 3-channel label (A,B,C) but just two switch positions (left, right). The manual instructs you to set your copter channel to match - yet the copter has no channel selector anywhere in its construction - not even a visible dip switch. (Maybe the copter was factory set to "C" but the remote only supported "A" or "B"?)

Fortunately, Amazon protects this purchase - thanks, Amazon. Returned.

-
Update: read my other reviews. I found success from Amazon reseller "Superstition Hobbies" and have enjoyed that S107 pair so much, I visited them to buy a third one as a gift. Best choice.

Also the face and hair of this doll are more true to Gal Gadot, the actress who played the part, so some of the magic of the movie is captured. As she comes she is HARDLY "Battle Ready!" It's easy once you figure it out and know what does what. Flying indoors is a bit of a challenge until you get a hold of it but outdoors it zips around like a hummingbird. text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Natural Play: Play, Draw, Create Reusable Drawing & Magnet Kit – Ocean (42 Magnets, 5 Dry-Erase Markers) I wanted to LOVE this set.
I really like it. But I don’t love it.

1st - I don’t know why companies create toys for kids 3+ that include markers that aren’t washable!!

2nd - the main (black) dry erase maker is the only one that is a complete handled marker with an eraser lid. The other 4 markers have a 1.5” handle area to hold onto. The markers work and erase well.
The markers are hard to get back into their elastic straps. It’s difficult to do as an adult- let alone a 3+yo. An additional 1/4” of elastic would have been helpful.

3rd - the activity pages have a spiral binding. The way it is set up the last page is attached to the back of the kit - I like this. But the spiral is too small to allow the pages to tuck behind the kit and the top of the pages lift up from the back of the bottom.
The pages are sometimes used together for a project but not always.

4th - there isn’t a bag or something to store the magnets that aren’t being used.
The magnets are all on 2 sheets and are very strong. You can easily layer these magnets to get different looks. There are 54 magnets so it would be nice if there was an area built in to store the magnets while they aren’t being used.

5th - This activity pad takes a lot of space and is larger than a child’s lap - it’s 23” wide. It would be nice if the pad could be opened and folded in half.

6th - the velcro closure is nice and strong but the cardboard tab is weaker than it needs to be. I worry that after much use this tab will be ripped off.

All that being said - this activity pad is nice.
It’s a good quiet time activity that has a lot of fun included.
My daughter takes this to restaurants and plane rides to keep her busy!
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Natural Play: Play, Draw, Create Reusable Drawing & Magnet Kit – Ocean (42 Magnets, 5 Dry-Erase Markers)

PlayMonster Farkle Frenzy Multi/None, 2 - 4 Player So I played Farkle a long time ago, and my family in another state has begun playing Farkle pretty regularly on family game nights. So I was excited to get Farkle Frenzy. But I have to admit we played the first four games with different rules each time as we figured them out (not sure that I have it completely correct now.) It is definitely not a true form of Farkle, but like I said, it's been a long time, but the scoring definitely is different. Not that that is completely bad. I just can't shake the feeling that I'm getting something wrong.

But as improvement to the game, the shared dice is great, the kids love to depress the bubble and can't wait for their turn to push it. The game board pyramid is also a nice addition in giving them somewhere to place the dice, but the score is difficult and beyond my 6 year old. But we had fun playing it in general and we are looking forward to taking it to Grandma's house where they fully understand Farkle.

Pros
+ Pushing the bubble on the shared dice was a big hit
+ Fast moving game
+ Captured the attention of the boys even if they didn't necessarily understand the scoring.

Cons
- A little confusing on the scoring

Summary
All in all a fun game, even if we are putting a bit of a spin on the game. The 3D game board adds to the interest of young kids and Farkle is a very playable and enjoyable game.
text_fidelity_b: PlayMonster Farkle Frenzy Multi/None, 2 - 4 Player

Kulipari enemy -“BATTALTIONS” Scorpion Ranger figure with gloved fist and deadly spear! This guy is a solid if not particularly exciting figure. It’s more of a collectible I suppose than a play figure, so I guess if you’re OK with that it serves its purpose.

You have the dimensions in the description, but to give a sense of size context, it’s almost exactly the size of a D-cell battery. Just slightly shorter and slightly broader. But picture a D-cell and you have a very good idea of size.

It’s plastic, with its two claw arms able to pivot at the shoulder a full circle. Nothing else is movable/posable on the body. The plastic feels a bit cheap, and there’s a mold residue on the tail. And the back is stamped with some words and numbers (Mattel, Made in China, etc.).

He stands solid on his two feet, tough to tip over forward, not so hard to tip over backwards. His hands can hold the large spear pretty firmly. The detailing is relatively minimal.

Again, as a collectible, I suppose it’s fine enough. For play purposes, in our family we strongly recommend figures from Schleich, Pago, or Carnegie, all of which are good sized, nicely detailed, and have an excellent build quality and heft to them. this has a different intent, so I can’t fault it for not meeting those same standards, but that’s just to give some context.
text_fidelity_b: Kulipari enemy -“BATTALTIONS” Scorpion Ranger figure with gloved fist and deadly spear!

Radio Flyer Air Ride Balance Bike, Toddler Bike, Ages 1.5-5 Pink , White It is assembled easily as mine seemed to come partially assembled beyond the scope of the directions.

It looks good, has a smooth ride, with a snazzy traditional bell to alert the neighbors.That's all good, but it needs more work at the design level.

The handlebars don't seem to attach securely, but not unsafely. A 3 year-old might not be able to loosen them, but any adult certainly can. Tighten them as hard as you can.

The cover for the handlebars -- where it attaches to the headset (just above the wheel) pops off whenever the wheel is turned. It is intended to, and does, snap in when still, but should remain snapped in always.

The bike is designed, per the packaging, for 2.5-5 year-olds. My boy turns 3 in three weeks and is considered average height. He's slightly too small. Instead, the age guidelines should describe height, not age, or both. He'll grow into it so I'm not concerned.

Overall, I'll keep it, but if I were to buy a new one, I'd buy one fully assembled, maybe even used, to ensure everything was solidly connected.

Anthony Trendl
TreeFortBooks.com

I’ve reviewed a number of them, and I can’t speak highly enough of their quality builds. They are made to last, even if roughly played with. We’ve had several now for about a decade, and they look no different than when they arrived, despite having gone through a number of dino “battles” and the like. This one is no exception. Once you move past the toddler years, though, that will be much less of an issue.

In terms of looks, it’s nicely painted (again, as usual with Schleich), with the blue cuts running down central area from head to tail tip standing out particularly nicely. The pose is as if it is about to take a step forward or perhaps step on something (someone?). The face is my one real complaint about this model. It’s a raw sort of red color, which isn’t all that aesthetic. It almost looks like it’s been flayed, or perhaps is furiously angry. And there’s something about the mouth being open in the manner it is that just seems a bit off-putting.But at least the teeth look like the right sort (I hate when one has, for instance, obviously carnivorous teeth on herbivores).

It’s nice to have a new model and a relatively unknown one at that. Outside of the head/face, which is a relatively minor complaint, the barapasuaruk is another fine addition to a great line of toys/models.

The Elsa’s Magical Castle model isn’t large, but it has loads of sparkle and detail; and tons of play potential in the many accessories (e,g., castle furniture, Olaf’s train) and moving parts (e,g., swirling staircase, snow slide). I love shiny stuff, and Elsa’s shimmering cape is something to behold. I also love trains, so Olaf’s train is another plus. The little snowmen’s teeter-totter (near the snow fort) is fun. I don’t really care for the scary snow monster, but it helps in reenacting scenes from the movie.

Some of the model’s sparkle is added with stickers, but there aren’t a lot of stickers, and they’re easy to apply. There is a moving slide that opens and closes the tall castle front doors. Klutz Bath and Body Activity Kit Multicolor, 9" Length x 1.75" Width x 9" Height When it comes to making things on our own, my household is a busy place with lots of creativity flowing. When we saw this kit, we could not wait to use it. Finally after waiting due to issues in our house which required a lot of remodeling, we were able to try this out. Let's see how it was..

WHAT IS THIS KIT LIKE?
This kit is one of our favorites. Being those who love color, we enjoyed the beautiful colored box. The box has a very detailed booklet on it which outlines every single project in the box and tells how to do the project. The photography is perfect and easy to read and follow. The layout and writing is perfect for using with children- both younger and older. There is not only an assortment of ingredients all carefully labeled and packaged, but there are little boxes and other decorative containers that you put together to give or display your creations in. I love that the bags are also labeled with what project it is good for and the page number in the booklet which is part of the box, so you won't lose it.

HOW DID OUR CREATIONS TURN OUT?
We had such fun with this. We enjoyed making the Bubble Bath Bon Bons most of all, and they really did work nicely in the tub. We have not done ALL of the projects yet, but the Bon Bons are the favorite so far- especially the marble method of mixing the colors. The little boxes that you put together are really cute and perfect to give as gifts. We also had fun with the lip mask.

ANY DRAWBACKS?
You will have to buy some fresh ingredients for this kit. That means that your treatments will be natural and safe for the face as well as fresh. Strawberry, lemon, avocado, banana, milk, honey, coconut milk, fine sugar or colored sugar, yogurt, and olive oil. Be prepared to have those on hand if you want to do the entire kit. We didn't mind though as we use these things in our home anyway, except for sugar, but I did have some on hand from a sugar scrub we experimented with in the past.

THE BOTTOM LINE
With all of the more unusual ingredients supplied, this kit is great fun to do. My daughter and I had a wonderful time with it. The colors, layout, and packaging are top notch. With the exception of having to provide quite a few fresh ingredients, this is easy and convenient but great fun when you finally do get to have your SPA day!

MY RATING
FIVE STARS! This can be used from young kids who are able to do this with supervision up to older kids- even late teens- who really want to have fun creating a spa day. I can also see using the principles used in this in the future creating a spa day for grandma or others that the kids want to reach out to for a special day.

KURATU LCD Writing Tablet Colorful Screen Toys for 3-12 Years Old Boys Girls,Drawing Board Reusable Doodle Board Drawing Pad Kids Electronic Education Systems (10 inch Black-S) This is yet another variation of the "Boogie Board" drawing tablet. If you are not familiar with the concept, it is NOT a digital tablet, but essentially a reusable drawing tool much like a whiteboard. It starts off as an opaque black surface that reveals a different color underneath with pressure. So you can draw on it using the included pen, a fingernail, or anything with enough pressure really, and then erase it all at once with the erase button on the bottom. The only electronics involved is a battery that "zaps" the display back to opaque to start over. This battery should last years as it only gets used when erasing for a split second.
I actually like this one better than some of our other ones as the contrast between the black and revealed color is quite high. Some of the inexpensive Boogie Board clones lack contrast and can be hard to see sometimes, but that is not the case here. It also seems to have a multi-colored background, so as you draw or write, it feels like the color is changing (really it is just revealing a different part of the material behind the LCD). I also really like the size of it, as our other drawing tablets were small whereas this one feels closer to a sheet of paper. My 12 year old son actually finds this comfortable for using as a scratch pad for his math homework, which is a great environmentally friendly alternative to scrap paper. And my younger kids like drawing pictures on it or playing games like tick-tack-toe.
You do have to be a little bit careful about resting your hand on it as it seems even that amount of pressure will leave a mark, and sadly you can't erase part of a picture, you can only erase the entire thing in one shot with the button. But this is true of all similar drawing pads due to how it works, so that is no fault of this product. As far as the Boogie Board clones go, this is my favorite so far.

text_fidelity_a:
SYMA Drone with Camera 1080P HD FPV Cameras Remote Control Toys RC Quadcopter Helicopter Gifts for Boys Girls Adults Beginners with Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, One Key Start, 3D Flips 2 Batteries Disclaimer: I own a DJI Mavic Pro, and started out with a Holy Stone quadcopter. I've flown smaller ones like the DJI Spark, which is similar in size. I would say that for the price, this is a five-star drone. You get a lot for $80.
Pros:
Small manageable size - the drone is large enough to make it feel like a nice machine, but small enough, especially when folded, to port around, which is nice because it lends itself to easy travel. You can also easily launch it and land it from and on your hand.

Robust and reasonably crash proof - The blade guards seemed kind of flimsy, and didn’t stay on well, so I flew without them. The drone handled test crashes well. The propellers held up well, with only some minor scrapes after hitting the ground and nearby trees. The copter simply hit the ground and the arms folded in on impact.

Quiet - The drone has a relatively quiet sound, and isn't too loud. I could talk to those next to me while flying without having to raise my voice while the copter was only a few feet away.

Auto-flip function - This is fun. When executed, the drone flips in your specified direction, rolling quickly left, right, forward or backward and returning to hovering once completed. The flip function does not work once the battery drops below a certain percentage.

LED lights for battery and connectivity - These are easy to see when on the ground and display info about the battery when charging or low, and connectivity when first powered on. The rear lights are green, and the ones in the front are red, but they can be hard to see in daylight once it gets more than about 30 feet away.

Good range. I flew the drone about 70 or 80 feet away laterally without any problems, and about 40 feet up before coming down for fear of wind gusts. It worked fine, with no noticeable latency.

Headless Mode - Great function for learning pilots, especially for a drone like this that has no camera feed. However, the instructions are quite confusing on how to engage this and it took me a solid 5 minutes of fiddling with the controls to get it to work. To get this to work, take off, hold the button at the top left of the controller until it starts beeping, and then push the stick forward. The forward-facing direction will remain that relative forward until this function is disengaged.

Tuning - This was easy to do, and I liked the tactility of the joystick buttons. I found it worked well.

Camera usability- The quality is good, and it is fun to use. However, I’m kind of in the middle on this, which is why the camera is in both the pros and cons. It does provide an accurate view of what the drone sees, and I didn’t have almost any lag. The picture resolution was nice. It’s not super easy to use, but I was able to figure out most of the controls while flying.

Battery: This had a nice battery life, with about 22 minutes of battery life to 1.5 hours charging time. I didn’t stream video, which I would imagine uses a bit more battery, bt for my medium intensity flight, I was very happy with the flight time, especially considering that they give you two batteries, which could give you about 45 minutes of flight time.

Cons:
Unstable/Jerky Camera - Because the camera is hard-mounted to the drone body, the video is very twitchy and jerky as the drone flies around and tilts, particularly when descending. The video became very shaky. I found myself more inclined to use the photo option over the video though, because of how unstable it was. I also found the field of view to be frustratingly narrow, and wanted a more upwards view from the drone.

Instructions aren't very clear - I found myself struggling to engage Headless mode, as well as set up the camera, one of the main selling points with this drone. I’ve found this is a common issue with Syma instructions, and it just makes the products a lot harder to use. There are occasional typos, and the layout is confusing.
text_fidelity_b: SYMA Drone with Camera 1080P HD FPV Cameras Remote Control Toys RC Quadcopter Helicopter Gifts for Boys Girls Adults Beginners with Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, One Key Start, 3D Flips 2 Batteries

AKAMATE Kids Action Camera Waterproof Video Digital Children Cam 1080P HD Sports Camera Camcorder for Boys Girls, Build-in 4Games, 32GB SD Card [[VIDEOID:3ab25a1fe74e640fbb16d3764ecc8aea]] This Kid's Action Camera was better than I expected. The camera (not in the waterproof case) measures 2.5" tall x 2.25" wide x 7/8" thick. The full color screen on the back measures 1.5" tall x 1.25" wide. The photographs can be up to 5M (you select can 5M, 3M, 2M, or 1M), and the photographs actually look pretty good (good color balance, no distortion, in focus). You can record just audio, and this came out clear when the camera was held within a foot distance of my mouth. I didn't test any further. The video can be selected at 1080P, 720P, or VGA quality. The 1080P looked good but it doesn't appear to be the normal HD proportions but rather closer to a square than a long rectangle. Some of the recordings also had mysterious sounds in addition to the expected ones--maybe like something tapped against the case during the recording. Also, I haven't found a way to remove the automatic time stamp placed on the video and photos. You can playback the videos, etc. on the camera if desired and also delete them off if the take was a bad one.

I found the camera very easy to use once I read the instructions. One rechargeable Li-ion battery is included. You charge the battery using the included USB cord connected to a computer or using a USB charging adapter. There's a red LED light when charging which turns off when it's full. Charging didn't take long, and they estimate that a full charge from near empty will take about 2.5 hours. I did notice that, even with the camera switched off in addition to being turned off, the battery tends to drain. We used the camera a bit, then left it sitting for a few weeks, only to discover that it needed to be fully recharged before we could use it again. So just charge it periodically so it'll always have enough of a charge.

They estimate that you can take about 90 minutes of 1080P video on the included 32 GB micro SD card (probably limited by the battery as I think 32GB can hold twice that). You need to format the micro SD card before use. You can do this by inserting the card into the camera, going to the settings menu, and selecting the option to format the card. You can download the images, audio, and video from the camera either through the USB cable (turn the camera on before connecting to your computer) or by removing the micro SD card and inserting it in the destination computer.

The set includes connectors that allow you to connect the camera to connectors that attach to a helmet, a bike, and so on. In the instructions, they show how the various connectors can be used for different situations. The set also comes in a very nice storage / carrying case so the unused connectors and such don't get lost. There is a holder for the camera that is a waterproof shell (good up to 30m or 98 feet underwater) and this can also be connected to all these other connectors.

I tried to film a sunset, and it did look pretty accurate when the lens was pointed directly at the sun/brightest area. If I dropped the focus of the camera to the ground, the camera Auto changed things so that it looked like a bright daylight scene. I tried some video of moving objects (like a flag on a windy day) or with me moving the camera, and it came out good.

The 3 games were pretty simple and may bore kids used to touchscreens. For example, the puzzle game would be pretty quick to work except you have to select a piece, use the arrow to move it one square, then select a piece, etc. Lots of clicking the buttons. Still, fun if there aren't other options around.
text_fidelity_b: AKAMATE Kids Action Camera Waterproof Video Digital Children Cam 1080P HD Sports Camera Camcorder for Boys Girls, Build-in 4Games, 32GB SD Card

Think Fun Mystic Market Strategy Card Game for 2-4 Players Ages 10 and Up – an Exciting Fast Paced Game Perfect for Both Families and Gamers, Multi I haven't gotten any feedback on this from the people I gave it to.. I would normally not bother with a review, but I thought it looked promising enough that it was worth recommending (even sight unseen, but I at least has opportunity to really look at it eventually, just not play it through). I bought it as a christmas gift for a couple of young boys- ages 10-14ish. Not entirely sure. When I am selecting gifts I always buy games or books for kids, always looking for educational offerings.. and given the theme of this and how it is designed for education in mind.. I thought this one seemed right up their ally. I had read reviews, looked over the details of the game, and while it cost a little more than I would normally spend on a token gift for kids I don't know real well, I thought it was interesting enough sounding to me- and educationally interesting that it would be worth a bit of a splurge (hoping they liked it and benefited from it!). Math, imagination, intrigue, magic, economics, strategy, skill development.. all UNPLUGGED- no need for apps, electronics. Can play under kitchen table light, or by candlelight. *I* thought it sounded fun. I may have to pick up another game for my own use at home.

I also liked the look of the box and the components. The colorful thick cards, bright potions in bottles on a rack, thick play currency.. It just didn't/doesn't look cheap. I was able to look over the materials, and it is a solid looking game. I just didn't have chance to actually play it. I really hope they liked it,and that the parents appreciated it. It seems like a game to hold on to, take care of and use time and time again.

It is because I am considering purchasing again for future gift giving, and have recommended other people to check it out, and that I keep it book marked to come back to, that I am going ahead with a full 5 star rating. It looks good, has quality look and feel, has game play with both education and imagination in mind. Instructions are straightforward- not too awkward or frustrating. The marketplace reminds me of any of the online game play (especially mmos) but all without the need to be attached to electronics.
text_fidelity_b: Think Fun Mystic Market Strategy Card Game for 2-4 Players Ages 10 and Up – an Exciting Fast Paced Game Perfect for Both Families and Gamers, Multi

text_fidelity_a:
eeBoo French Flash Cards I had the great fortune of parents who made sure I learned three other languages as a kid. They started very early with me and I distinctly remember them making their own flashcards. It's too bad that they didn't have access to these beautiful, affordable, and very easy to use flashcards to aid them! Now, as a parent, teacher, and a nanny, I work hard to teach my kids the basics of French and Spanish, and I stumbled across these. They have been well worth the price and they were highly affordable. Best of all, my kids that I teach love the cards and enjoy using them too. I would recommend them to both the beginner and the advanced speaker as they embark on teaching others.

There are a few times that the cards use outdated pronunciations or word choices, but it's actually a plus in my book because it aids further in teaching. When I see a card with a different context of pronunciation or word choice than what is currently popular or commonly used, then I can supplement by saying "Or you could say it like this ..." Anyways, the cards are really lovely and sturdy. Venn Board Game | Family Game for 2+ Players | Cooperative & Competitive Gameplay Variations | Creative Word Association Game Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Ages 10+ Venn is a party game that plays a large number of players, and it comes with a competitive mode and a cooperative mode. The cooperative mode was not fun for our family, so we'll focus on the competitive game. In this game, you use cards with odd artwork to get your teammates to guess a set of three out of twelve possible games. The cards go in one of the seven different sections of a three-way Venn Diagram like you used to see in school. Using the clues you're given, you attempt to identify the three chosen words that the card placer is going for.

There are some fun times to be had here, but a few problems as well. The art is meant to be odd and unusual, but a good amount of it is just plain bad - characters are off-center, objects look like they're floating in the background, etc - and the cards are hard to use because they don't actually fit inside the sections of the Venn diagram. The words are usually very descriptive, but there are also some bad word chocies in the deck like "great" or "interesting" which could literally mean anything.

Unfortunately, this is competing in a crowded market - competitive, team-based family games have been done to death, so if you want to stand out, choose a game like Codenames or Just One or So Clover or...well, there's a lot of them, and they're mostly better than this.
text_fidelity_b: Venn Board Game | Family Game for 2+ Players | Cooperative & Competitive Gameplay Variations | Creative Word Association Game Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Ages 10+
